cards.title: Quasipolynomial AC⁰ self-learning
cards.formal: Does AC⁰ admit uniform quasipolynomial-size AC⁰ self-learners? More precisely, for every fixed integers d,k≥1 and fixed rational constants ε,δ∈(0,1/100], do there exist constants D,a≥1 and a uniform family of randomized multi-output oracle AC⁰ circuits Lₙ, of depth at most D and total size at most Q(n)=2^{a⌈log₂(n+2)⌉^a}, such that for every n≥1 and every Boolean function f on n bits with an AC⁰ circuit of depth at most d and at most n^k gates, Lₙ with membership-query oracle f outputs an effective description of a depth-at-most-D AC⁰ hypothesis h of size at most Q(n), with Pr[Pr_{x uniform in {0,1}ⁿ}[h(x)≠f(x)]≤ε]≥1−δ? The outer probability is over the learner’s independent fair random input bits. This is the fixed-constant learning-parameter reading of the source’s self-learning question.
cards.why: Tests whether learning a shallow Boolean computation intrinsically needs stronger gates or greater depth than evaluating it. The restriction links learning complexity with the circuit complexity of approximate minimization and with derandomization, beyond the usual sequential running-time measure.
cards.status_note: Read the conference definition and question, the full ECCC report dated 3 July 2018 and the later thesis discussion. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no resolution in this exact learner-and-hypothesis model; they are not exhaustive. The thesis is dated Trinity 2020 on its title page, despite later repository indexing dates.

sentences: The target is to learn any polynomial-size constant-depth Boolean circuit using a constant-depth learner of quasipolynomial size.
The learner can query the unknown function and uses random bits, with approximation measured on uniform inputs.
Its output must itself describe a quasipolynomial-size constant-depth AND/OR/NOT circuit.
Known sequential-time learning and threshold-augmented self-learning do not give this combination.
The card states the source’s fixed-constant accuracy and confidence interpretation and records the same question in a 2020 thesis.

cards.definitions:
An AC⁰ circuit is a finite Boolean directed acyclic circuit with unbounded-fan-in AND and OR gates, unary NOT gates, constants 0 and 1, and input bits. Depth is the greatest number of gates on a directed input-to-output path. Circuit descriptions may be nonuniform for the target function: the guarantee covers every eligible f at each length, not merely one uniformly generated target family. Neither majority/threshold gates nor parity gates are added to the basis.

For the learner, an oracle gate has n ordered Boolean inputs y₁,…,yₙ and returns the bit f(y₁,…,yₙ). Each oracle gate counts as one gate in the depth; its query wires count in the size. Query bits may depend on answers at earlier gates, but the total circuit depth remains bounded by D. The learner is a circuit with multiple output bits and at most Q(n) independent fair random input bits; there is no further source of information about f. Size here bounds gates, wires, input terminals and output terminals together. The number of random bits and all circuit topology are fixed before f is supplied. No unrestricted computation is allowed between queries. The accuracy distribution is uniform on the target’s entire n-bit domain, independently of the learner’s coins. This is not distribution-free PAC learning and does not require a fixed output or fixed queries on most random tapes.

An effective output is an explicit layered description of a Boolean AC⁰ circuit on n bits. One concrete convention uses D ordered layers of padded gate slots, a gate-type field for each slot, Boolean adjacency masks to earlier layers or input terminals, and an output-selector mask. NOT slots have exactly one predecessor; all edges go to later layers. Unused slots are constants. The format has polynomial length in the number of slots, and evaluating a valid encoded circuit on an input is possible by an AC⁰ circuit of depth O(D) and polynomial size in the encoding length. Both the description length and hypothesis gates/wires are bounded by Q(n); invalid descriptions count as failures. Enlarging a and D absorbs the polynomial overhead of this explicit encoding and standard layering. The output h has no f-oracle gates. A constant-depth circuit with only one additional top threshold gate would not meet the stated hypothesis class.

Uniformity means that, for the fixed d,k,ε,δ, one deterministic Turing algorithm given 1ⁿ generates the entire description of Lₙ in time polynomial in Q(n). The algorithm, its polynomial exponent, D and a may depend on those four fixed parameters, but not on n or f. There is no advice depending on f and no claim of polynomial-time generation in n. The source explicitly leaves general ε,δ dependence informal and often fixes sufficiently small constants; the statement adopts that constant-parameter interpretation. It does not demand a single learner whose complexity is polynomial in 1/ε and log(1/δ), nor learner or hypothesis depth equal to target depth. All bounds apply to every n; constant padding can handle small lengths.
cards.answer_criterion: A positive answer supplies the uniform oracle-circuit families and proves all depth, size, encoding and probability guarantees for every fixed d,k,ε,δ in the specified ranges and every eligible target. A negative answer disproves this universal existence claim, for example for some fixed parameter choice against all permitted learner depths and quasipolynomial size exponents. Quasipolynomial sequential running time, unrestricted hypothesis circuits, or a threshold-augmented hypothesis class alone do not meet the target.

context_blocks.title: Learning has its own circuit complexity
context_blocks.text: Self-learning compares the resources needed to infer a function with those needed to evaluate it. The source requires both the learning computation and the generated hypothesis to stay in the same gate class, while allowing larger size and a larger constant depth.

context_blocks.title: Known time bounds leave this question
context_blocks.text: The source distinguishes this question from known deterministic quasipolynomial-time learning of AC⁰. A sequential time bound does not supply an AC⁰ learner or an AC⁰ representation of its answer.

context_blocks.title: A nearby threshold-augmented class
context_blocks.text: The 2018 paper observes subexponential self-learning for a class with one majority gate over AC⁰ circuits. Rajgopal’s thesis develops the related threshold-over-AC⁰ result and its consequences for approximate circuit minimization. These are different gate classes and size bounds.

context_blocks.title: A later explicit open question
context_blocks.text: The conclusion of Chapter 3 of Rajgopal’s 2020 thesis again asks for quasipolynomial AC⁰ learners for AC⁰. It therefore does not present the threshold-augmented result as a solution of this question.

cards.context:
Self-learning compares the resources needed to infer a function with those needed to evaluate it. The source requires both the learning computation and the generated hypothesis to stay in the same gate class, while allowing larger size and a larger constant depth.

The source distinguishes this question from known deterministic quasipolynomial-time learning of AC⁰. A sequential time bound does not supply an AC⁰ learner or an AC⁰ representation of its answer.

The 2018 paper observes subexponential self-learning for a class with one majority gate over AC⁰ circuits. Rajgopal’s thesis develops the related threshold-over-AC⁰ result and its consequences for approximate circuit minimization. These are different gate classes and size bounds.

The conclusion of Chapter 3 of Rajgopal’s 2020 thesis again asks for quasipolynomial AC⁰ learners for AC⁰. It therefore does not present the threshold-augmented result as a solution of this question.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. Our primary goal is a benchmark of 500 problems. Top 100 is a priority subset of those same 500, with secondary editorial attention. Both use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The existing Top 1000 view is not an active benchmark goal. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The legacy Top 1000 view has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The primary target is 500 problems; Top 100 is its priority subset with secondary editorial attention. Top 100, Top 500 and the legacy Top 1000 view use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.
